title: Inductors and Inductance Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav pulls the plug of a running mixer and a tiny blue spark jumps at the socket. Where did a spark strong enough to jump through air come from? From a coil inside the motor. In this animated lesson we meet the inductor, a coil of wire, its symbol (air core and iron core), and the magnetic field that passes through every turn.

On a live breadboard two lamps race: the one with a resistor lights at once, the one with a coil brightens slowly while the oscilloscope draws its current rising in a smooth curve. Open the switch and the scope shows a sharp voltage spike across the coil, the same spike behind the spark. We derive NΦ = LI, L = NΦ/I and the induced EMF ε = -L dI/dt (Lenz's law), meet the henry, then see what decides L for a long coil: L = μ₀μrN²A/l with μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ H/m. We compare air core, iron core (choke), ferrite core and variable inductors and work out the inductance of a 500 turn coil. Then the exam trap (L grows as N², not N), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 29 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 4: Passive Electronic Components (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
